subject: maths
title: Primary 2 Fractions
seo_title: P2 Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Fraction as part of a whole; notation; comparing and ordering unit fractions and like fractions (denominators not exceeding 12)
meta_desc: Free P2 maths practice: equal parts, naming the fraction shaded, unit fractions, and comparing and ordering fractions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A fraction needs equal parts: the bottom number counts all the parts, the top number counts the parts you take.
key_sub: 3 of 8 equal parts shaded = 3/8. More parts means smaller parts, so 1/8 < 1/4.
body_html:
Equal parts

A fraction is a part of a whole. The parts must be equal (the same size).

Name the fraction

Count all the equal parts. That is the bottom number, the denominator. Count the shaded parts. That is the top number, the numerator.

Equal partsEach part isWe write
2one half12
4one quarter14
5one fifth15
10one tenth110

Unit fractions: more parts, smaller parts

A unit fraction has 1 on top, like 14 or 18. When the same whole is cut into more parts, each part is smaller.

Example

Which is greater, 13 or 19?

Thirds are bigger parts than ninths.

Answer: 13

Compare and order like fractions

Like fractions have the same denominator, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators.

Example

Arrange 59, 29, 79 from the smallest to the greatest.

The denominators are the same. Order the numerators: 2, 5, 7.

Answer: 29, 59, 79

Example

Arrange 13, 18, 15 from the smallest to the greatest.

The numerators are all 1. The biggest denominator is the smallest fraction.

Answer: 18, 15, 13

Word problems: draw a model

Draw a bar for the whole. Cut it into equal units. The number of units is the denominator.

Example

Mrs Lim cut a cake into 8 equal pieces. Wei Ming ate 3 pieces. What fraction of the cake did he eat?

The cake is 8 units. He ate 3 units.

Answer: 38

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 2 unequal parts “halves”Check that the parts are the same size
18 > 14 (because 8 > 4)More parts means smaller parts: 18 < 14
3 of 8 parts shaded, writing 58The top number counts the shaded parts: 38
3 of 8 parts shaded, writing 35The bottom number counts all the parts: 38
Counting the lines, not the partsA strip with 4 cuts has 5 parts

faq.q: What is taught in P2 fractions?
faq.a: In Primary 2, students learn that a fraction is a part of a whole cut into equal parts, and how to write it with a numerator and denominator. They compare and order unit fractions and like fractions with denominators up to 12.

faq.q: How do I explain fractions to my child?
faq.a: Fold a paper strip into equal parts and colour some of them. Count all the parts for the bottom number and the coloured parts for the top number: 3 coloured parts out of 8 is 3/8.
When the same whole is cut into 8 equal parts instead of 4, each part is smaller. So 1/8 < 1/4, even though 8 is bigger than 4. This is the most common P2 fraction mistake.

faq.q: Is fractions in the MOE syllabus for Primary 2?
faq.a: Yes. Fraction as part of a whole, fraction notation, and comparing and ordering unit and like fractions are part of the Primary 2 Standard Mathematics syllabus (MOE 2021). In Primary 3, students go on to equivalent fractions.

items.q: Which shape is cut into halves?
items.e: Halves are 2 equal parts. That is D. A has 2 parts, but they are not equal. B has 3 equal parts. C has 2 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is cut into thirds?
items.e: Thirds are 3 equal parts. That is A. B has 3 parts, but they are not equal. C has 4 equal parts. D has 3 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is cut into quarters?
items.e: Quarters are 4 equal parts. That is C. A has 4 parts, but they are not equal. B has 3 equal parts. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into sixths?
items.e: Sixths are 6 equal parts. That is B. A has 6 parts, but they are not equal. C has 8 equal parts. D has 4 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into fifths?
items.e: Fifths are 5 equal parts. That is B. A has 5 parts, but they are not equal. C has 6 equal parts. D has 4 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is not cut into equal parts?
items.e: Look for parts of different sizes. That is D. A has 4 equal parts. B has 3 equal parts. C has 5 equal parts.

items.q: How many equal parts is the circle cut into?
items.e: Count the parts, not the lines. All the parts are the same size. There are 5 equal parts.

items.q: How many equal parts is the strip cut into?
items.e: The strip has 4 parts, but they are not the same size. So they are not equal parts. We cannot use them to make a fraction.

items.q: How many equal parts is the rectangle cut into?
items.e: Count the parts, not the lines. All the parts are the same size. There are 6 equal parts.

items.q: How many equal parts is the square cut into?
items.e: The square has 2 parts, but they are not the same size. So they are not equal parts. We cannot use them to make a fraction.

items.q: The strip is cut into 6 equal parts. What fraction of the whole is 1 part?
items.e: There are 6 equal parts, so each part is one sixth: 16. The bottom number is the number of equal parts.

items.q: The rectangle is cut into 8 equal parts. What fraction of the whole is 1 part?
items.e: There are 8 equal parts, so each part is one eighth: 18. The bottom number is the number of equal parts.

items.q: The circle is cut into 7 equal parts. What fraction of the whole is 1 part?
items.e: There are 7 equal parts, so each part is one seventh: 17. The bottom number is the number of equal parts.

items.q: The strip is cut into 10 equal parts. What fraction of the whole is 1 part?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts, so each part is one tenth: 110. The bottom number is the number of equal parts.

items.q: How many eighths make 1 whole?
items.e: One whole cut into eighths has 8 equal parts. So 8 eighths make 1 whole: 88 = 1.

items.q: How many twelfths make 1 whole?
items.e: One whole cut into twelfths has 12 equal parts. So 12 twelfths make 1 whole: 1212 = 1.

items.q: A shape is cut into 3 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 3 equal parts are called thirds. Each part is one third: 13.

items.q: Mei Ling cuts a paper strip into 2 parts. One part is longer than the other. Is each part a half?
items.e: Halves must be 2 equal parts. One part is longer, so they are not halves.

items.q: What fraction of the strip is shaded?
items.e: There are 3 equal parts in all. 2 are shaded. So 23 of the strip is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: There are 5 equal parts in all. 2 are shaded. So 25 of the circle is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: There are 6 equal parts in all. 1 is shaded. So 16 of the rectangle is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the strip is shaded?
items.e: There are 8 equal parts in all. 3 are shaded. So 38 of the strip is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: There are 6 equal parts in all. 5 are shaded. So 56 of the circle is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: There are 9 equal parts in all. 4 are shaded. So 49 of the rectangle is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the strip is shaded?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts in all. 7 are shaded. So 710 of the strip is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?

items.q: What fraction of the strip is shaded?

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: There are 12 equal parts in all. 7 are shaded. So 712 of the circle is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is not shaded?
items.e: There are 5 equal parts. 3 are shaded, so 2 are not shaded. The answer is 25.

items.q: What fraction of the strip is not shaded?
items.e: There are 8 equal parts. 5 are shaded, so 3 are not shaded. The answer is 38.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is not shaded?
items.e: There are 6 equal parts. 4 are shaded, so 2 are not shaded. The answer is 26.

items.q: Which shape has 35 shaded?
items.e: 35 needs 5 equal parts with 3 shaded. That is B. A shows 25. C has 6 parts, so it shows 36. D has 5 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape has 23 shaded?
items.e: 23 needs 3 equal parts with 2 shaded. That is D. A shows 13. B has 3 parts, but they are not equal. C has 4 parts, so it shows 24.

items.q: Which fraction is two fifths?
items.e: Two fifths means 2 parts out of 5 equal parts. The 2 goes on top and the 5 goes at the bottom: 25.

items.q: In 49, what does the 9 tell you?
items.e: The bottom number (the denominator) tells you how many equal parts make the whole: 9. The top number (the numerator) tells you how many parts we take: 4.

items.q: In 511, which number is the numerator?
items.e: The numerator is the top number: 5. The denominator is the bottom number: 11.

sets.title: Unit fractions: more parts, smaller parts

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Look at the shaded parts. The bar cut into the fewest parts has the longest part. Fewer parts means bigger parts. The answer is 12.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Look at the shaded parts. The bar cut into the most parts has the shortest part. More parts means smaller parts. The answer is 110.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Look at the shaded parts. The bar cut into the fewest parts has the longest part. Fewer parts means bigger parts. The answer is 13.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Look at the shaded parts. The bar cut into the most parts has the shortest part. More parts means smaller parts. The answer is 112.

items.q: Which is the greatest: 15, 112, 13, 19?
items.e: All the numerators are 1. The smallest denominator gives the biggest parts. The greatest is 13.

items.q: Which is the smallest: 16, 14, 110, 17?
items.e: All the numerators are 1. The biggest denominator gives the smallest parts. The smallest is 110.

items.e: All the numerators are 1. The biggest denominator gives the smallest parts. The smallest is 112.

items.q: Which is true?
c: 110 > 12
18 > 14
14 > 18
16 > 13
items.e: A whole cut into 4 parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 8 parts. So 14 > 18.

items.q: Which is correct?
c: 19 < 16
13 < 15
14 < 17
12 < 112
items.e: More parts means smaller parts. Ninths are smaller than sixths, so 19 < 16.

items.q: Which one is true?
c: 16 > 12
17 > 15
15 > 111
112 > 110
items.e: Fifths are bigger than elevenths (fewer parts, bigger parts). So 15 > 111.

items.q: Which unit fraction is greater than 16?
items.e: A unit fraction is greater when its denominator is smaller. 5 is smaller than 6, so 15 > 16.

items.q: Which unit fraction is smaller than 15?
items.e: A unit fraction is smaller when its denominator is bigger. 8 is bigger than 5, so 18 < 15.

items.q: A cake is cut into more equal pieces. What happens to each piece?
items.e: The same cake is shared into more pieces, so each piece is smaller. That is why 18 is smaller than 14.

items.q: Kavya says 110 is greater than 15 because 10 is greater than 5. Is she right?
c: No, 15 is greater
items.e: A whole cut into 10 parts has smaller parts than a whole cut into 5. So 15 > 110.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole cut into 6 equal parts has 6 sixths. All 6 parts make the whole: 66 = 1.

items.q: How do you compare 411 and 711?
items.e: Both fractions are elevenths, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: 7 > 4, so 711 > 411.

items.q: Mrs Lim cut a pandan cake into 8 equal pieces. Wei Ming ate 3 pieces. What fraction of the cake did he eat?
items.e: Draw the cake as 8 equal units. Wei Ming ate 3 units. So he ate 38 of the cake.

items.q: A pizza was cut into 6 equal slices. Ali’s family ate 4 slices. What fraction of the pizza was left?
items.e: 6 units − 4 units = 2 units left. So 26 of the pizza was left.

items.q: Siti, Raju, Chloe and Hafiz have water bottles of the same size. Siti drank 25 of her water, Raju drank 45, Chloe drank 15 and Hafiz drank 35. Who drank the most?
items.e: All the bars have 5 equal units. Raju’s bar has the most units shaded: 4. 45 is the greatest, so Raju drank the most.

items.q: On Sports Day, Arjun ran 710 km, Nurul ran 310 km, Ethan ran 910 km and Priya ran 510 km. Who ran the shortest distance?
items.e: All the distances are in tenths. Compare the numerators: 7, 3, 9 and 5. 3 is the smallest, so Nurul ran the shortest distance.

items.q: Four pizzas are the same size. Ahmad’s pizza is cut into 6 equal slices, Sarah’s into 3, Kumar’s into 8 and Xin Yi’s into 4. Each child eats 1 slice of their own pizza. Who eats the biggest slice?
items.e: Sarah’s pizza has the fewest slices, so each slice is the biggest. 13 is the greatest of 16, 13, 18, 14. Sarah eats the biggest slice.

items.q: Hui Min and Jun Jie are painting two walls of the same size. Hui Min has painted 512 of her wall. Jun Jie has painted 712 of his wall. Who has painted less?
items.e: Both fractions are twelfths, so compare the numerators: 5 < 7. 512 < 712, so Hui Min painted less.

items.q: Mdm Wong cut a ribbon into 5 equal pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is 1 piece?
items.e: The ribbon is cut into 5 equal pieces. 1 piece is one fifth: 15. (She made 4 cuts, but there are 5 pieces.)

items.q: Zhi Hao read 110 of a storybook. Kumar read 15 of the same storybook. Who read more?
c: Zhi Hao, as tenths are bigger
Kumar, as 15 > 110
items.e: A whole cut into 5 parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 10 parts. 15 > 110, so Kumar read more.

items.q: Ryan cut a watermelon into 10 equal slices. He gave 3 slices to his friends. What fraction of the watermelon did he give away?
items.e: There are 10 equal slices. Ryan gave away 3 of them. So he gave away 310 of the watermelon.

items.q: For Children’s Day, Mrs Ng has four ribbons. The red ribbon is 12 m long, the blue ribbon is 15 m long, the green ribbon is 13 m long and the yellow ribbon is 18 m long. Which ribbon is the shortest?
items.e: All the numerators are 1. The biggest denominator gives the smallest part. 18 is the smallest of 12, 15, 13, 18, so the yellow ribbon is the shortest.

items.q: Devi folded a paper strip into 9 equal parts. She coloured 4 parts red and the rest blue. What fraction of the strip is blue?
items.e: 9 units − 4 units = 5 units are blue. So 59 of the strip is blue.

items.q: A community garden plot is cut into 12 equal parts. 5 parts are for kangkong and the rest are for chilli. What fraction of the plot is for chilli?
items.e: 12 units − 5 units = 7 units are for chilli. So 712 of the plot is for chilli.

items.q: Farah, Arjun, Mei Ling and Ryan each have a bar of chocolate of the same size. Farah ate 13 of her bar, Arjun ate 16, Mei Ling ate 12 and Ryan ate 112. Who ate the least?
items.e: All the numerators are 1. Ryan’s bar is cut into the most parts (12), so 112 is the smallest. Ryan ate the least.

items.q: Mr Rahman cut a tray of kueh into 6 equal pieces. Ali ate 1 piece and his sister ate 2 pieces. What fraction of the tray of kueh did they eat altogether?
items.e: 1 unit + 2 units = 3 units out of 6 equal units. So they ate 36 of the tray.
